newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares climb to record on corporate news.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares climb to record on corporate news.

text.p: A spate of upbeat corporate news pushed leading Russian shares to a record close on Monday and traders expected continued upward movement, though not necessarily on Tuesday.
The Russian Trading System (RTS) 22-share index closed at 369.00 after 364.78 on Friday. Its previous record was 366.80 on May 19. Reported market volume was a healthy total $55.0 million.
Creditanstalt trader Andrei Galperin said he expected a correction from the quick rise, but that new money on the market could jump on lower prices and lead the market higher.
"There will not be sharp growth tomorrow, but there is a lot of money on the market," he said.

UCB trader Dmitry Yevenko said domestic funds leaving the Treasury bill market, where yields are now generally under 20 percent, would spur the market. "We do not expect the market to fall and I even expect a certain growth," he said.
Profit-taking in the last half hour of trade shaved off some of Monday's gains.
Traders said a large Western investor had sold a large block of national electric company UES EESR.RTS, spurring late selling. It closed at $0.3110 after $0.3159 on Friday.
Mosenergo MSNG.RTS received a credit rating and announced profits had grown by half in 1996 according to international accounts. It rose to $1.268 from $1.259.
LUKoil LKOH.RTS oil producer, announcing higher first quarter earnings to Russian accounting standards, rose to $16.10 from $15.72.
Rostelekom RTKM.RTS eased to $3.76 from $3.81 after it said that transfer of its controlling stake to holding company Svyazinvest had been completed.
